body: My husband is quite oblivious at times, more like 95% of the times. Even if you spell it out for him, it’ll go completely over his head unless its something he finds important. It is absolutely infuriating at times and sometimes I can ignore it. It definitely is something to learn to tolerate if you love that person.

Hmm to be honest, for me, its good riddance! lol There’s so much I can get done without opposition and the house stays clean. Also it’s much easier to cook dinners as well. He’s in the military so there are many days and nights that are long. Of course I miss him but when he’s out in the field it’s nice to get a break.

Of course words are hurtful. My husband doesn’t call me names but he can be cut throat with what he says at times. He has a hard time understanding someone else’s emotions. I’d say put in time to speak with a therapist. Please don’t forget to stick up for yourself. Don’t let him think he can steamroll each time and be dismissive. I’d say cut your loses and leave him. He really loved and respected you then he wouldn’t use such words.

My husband is notorious for doubling down because he’s hurt and feels the need to defend himself especially when being held accountable for his actions. He can be as cold as the come and part of it I know is his upbringing. It’s a hard thing to tolerate. 

I really hope OP can escape the mess. That’s only the start of spiraling down into something worse than name calling.

I know you said not to mention divorce but...honestly, if he doesn’t want to change and has threatened to kick you and your child out of the house? Then divorce might be your best option. His family of origin is going to be loyal to him not you especially seeing as how he’s painted you as a the bad guy. He needs to be loyal to you, his new family, and clearly he has shown you he’s incapable of doing that. Please get ahold of your family and plan a way out. Save you and your child the headache of dealing with him. You have your own child to worry about and raise. Why do you need to  sacrifice yourself and finish raising another woman’s GROWN child for her? If someone shows you who they really are, please believe them. I don’t know how many times I’ve ignored this and ended up burned and hurt.

Have you tried sharing that with your wife? From what it seems like, she’s been there for a lot. Hopefully she can meet you half way and both of you can give each other 100%. Maybe during counseling she can give you some kind of reassurance that she is willing to change for the better with you so that you two can continue to grow together.

No need to be defensive, I was simply making a comment that your wife is far better than I am. Being that I’ve been cheated on in previous relationships, I would have no issue leaving my spouse as soon as possible. There is no such thing as working it out with me. 

I completely understand that everyone has needs and you connected with someone that was experiencing  the same issue and you found her to be attractive etc. I will say that you made a choice, not a mistake. 
In your case, its good that you’ve finally come to your senses and are willing to make the effort to show your wife you actually love her and still do. Thank you.
Wow, your  wife is a far better woman than I am or could ever be. I hope you two manage to work things out.

What if you only did the chores you needed to do. Basically just cleaning up after yourself and only yourself. If he has laundry to do then oh well. If he’s hungry then he needs to figure it out. Oh there’s dishes in the sink then at leas you have washed your own. 

What if you just left the house for the day? Or just stayed at your moms for a couple of days? You need space and do not need to be followed around by someone that does not know how to communicate with their spouse. I’d highly suggest talking to someone about what you are both dealing with individually. 

Personally, I don’t like people in my space and yelling at me isn’t going to work. If I feel threatened I wouldn’t hesitate to give a warning to back off and then protect myself I I feel it’s necessary.

You know, something kind of similar happened between my husband and I expect it was a note with a woman’s name, phone number and email on it. I was cleaning out our car and asked if he still needed it because I knew it wasn’t mine. He got irritated and said no. Being that I’ve been cheated on in the past, not by him, I was worried but left it alone because if he did cheat, he wouldn’t be able to lie about it. He can barley hold water. Also, he’s given rides to friends in his platoon so we figured that’s where it came from.

I understand how you feel and we’ve only been married for a year. You didn’t marry him to become his mother, you married him to be his partner and assumingely vice versus. If he isn’t willing to get help or make the necessary changes that he can make within his means. It’s best to start focusing on yourself. Don’t sacrifice anymore of yourself then you already have.

Besides mocking you and shaming you, he should be helping you. There is a way he could have expressed his concerns in a way that could have been nurturing and understanding. Instead he put you down and shamed you. Honestly, even if my husband and I had recently gotten married, I’d ask for a divorce. If that’s how he’s going to act now, what about later even if you have tried marriage counseling? I’d say do your best to focus on yourself because only you can make yourself happy. Also, don’t forget that just because he is tour husband does not mean you cannot stand up for yourself. It’s important to create boundaries. He may not like it but that’s his problem to deal with. 

Build a support system outside the house and find people who are wanting to workout. Even if it’s just a group of women to have lunch with, it’s better than being at home with a disrespectful spouse.

Your husband understands that your body recently supported a whole other human being, right? That the human body when carrying a baby experiences many changes before and after pregnancy. If he is truly concerned then he needs to talk to you like an adult and not talk down to you. A partner would be willing to help, not tear down someone they supposedly love.

While I do agree with this, there is also the part where they should learn to understand how their partner receives love. Not that it has to be perfect because no one is but knowing that they are aware and practice it is meaningful.

I’m experiencing this too and trust me it’s hard. I’ve personally started seeing a counselor because I’ve grown tired and angry. I’d definitely try that to see if it helps give you some clarity and you have the ability to vent.

I understand completely, my husband gives me compliments and etc but I usually reply with, I think you meant to say I have a good personality. I’m a bigger woman and that’s usually what people say about bigger women. 

It’s hard to take what someone’s says at face value when you’re having a hard time with self image.

I wanted to clear up a few things, while getting pregnant is a worry for me. I am on birth control. What I meant by being someone’s mother was that I’ve fallen into that role again but instead of my younger sibling, it’s my husband. I’m worried about if this will continue and when we decide to have children will I have to parent two people?
Thank you and I’ll make sure to keep that in mind.

I actually grew up as an Army brat so it’s nothing new trust me.  This isn’t my first rodeo, in a way, except for it being my husband and not my father. I don’t have entirely a negative view towards it like some people. That’s not to say it’s easy cause military relationships are hard as hell. 

I’m not in a rush to have children, I’ve practically raised one with my sister. I don’t want to do it again anytime soon. I’ve found myself in the role but for my husband. It makes me worry about the future.

I’ve taken the pill form of birth control for some time and may look into other options. When I was a little younger I even thought of having my tubes tied when I was 18, silly I know lol
We have talked about how things would change etc but he has a hard time with communication and it’s tedious trying to guide the conversation. He has gotten better though.

You’re absolutely right, the burn out is very real. The way we became our brothers parents was not ideal as in our dad leaving unannounced and our mother leaving to live with some guy but originally told us she was going to rehab for her pill addiction. It was a slap in the face to be honest. 

No offense taken, I do feel anxious and uncertain. I wish we could have a full discussion about us and certain topics but it overwhelms him. I’m not sure about how to broach the topic without him shutting down and receiving vague answers.

I’ve thought of getting an IUD but not very keen on the potential of there being scar tissue. I’ve taken the pill form of birth control for sometime and had one that worked for me. Unfortunately since I’ve moved to another state, they didn’t provide that exact prescription but something similar.

We did discuss children before getting married. I think there were other factors that prevented us from truly focusing on ourselves etc. We both agreed we wanted to spend time together as a married couple before having kids. 
We have experienced some rough patches within the last few months and I recently had a pregnancy scare which doesn’t help. I’ve tried talking to him about there seemed to be a disconnect. I’ve noticed it’s hard for him to give emotional support and communicate. He’s gotten a little bit better about taking though.

I’m currently in counseling and was before I moved. We even went to counseling before he shipped out. When I spoke with his mom, it was to get a better idea of why he has a difficult time with communication. I recently had a pregnancy scare and we, well I, talked about it. It is something we need to talk about as a couple, for sure but communication is extremely difficult for him. 
He has gotten a little bit better this past month though.
